content:
[Intro]
[C]

[Verse 1]
Early one mor-
ning while
making the rounds
I
took a shot of co-
caine and I
[G]shot my woman
down I
went right
home and I
went to
bed I
[C]stuck that loving
forty four be-
neath my head

[Verse 2]
[C]Got up next
morning and I
grabbed that gun
Took a shot of co-
caine and a-
[G]way I run
Made a good
run but I
run too
slow They
[C]overtook me
down in Juarez,
Mexico

[Verse 3]
[C]Late in the
hot joints
taking the pills
In walked the
sheriff from
[G]Jericho Hill
He
said, "Willy
Lee, your name is
not Jack
Brown You're
[C]the dirty
hack that shot your
woman down"

[Verse 4]
[C]Said "Yes, oh
yes, my name is
Willy Lee
If
you've got the
warrant just a-
[G]read it to me
Shot her down
because she
made me
slow I
[C]thought I was her
daddy but she
had five more."

[Verse 5]
[C]
When I was arres-
ted I was
dressed in black,
They
put me on a
train and they
[G]took me back
Had no
friend for to
go my bail
They
[C]slapped my dried up
carcass in that
county jail

[Verse 6]
[C]Early next
morning about a
half past nine
I spied the
sheriff coming
[G]down the line
Talked and he coughed
as he
cleared his throat
He said, "Come
[C]on you dirty
hack into that
district court"

[Verse 7]
[C]Into the court-
room, my
trial began
Where I was
handled by
[G]twelve honest
men
Just be-
fore the jury
started out
I
[C]saw that little judge
commence to
look about

[Verse 8]
[C]
In about five
minutes,
in walked the man
Holding the
verdict in
[G]his right hand
The
verdict read,
in the
first degree
I
[C]hollered, "Lawdy,
Lawdy, have
mercy on me"

[Verse 9]
[C]The judge he
smiled as he
picked up his pin
Ninetynine
years in the
[G]Folsom Pen
Ninetynine
years under-
neath that ground
I
[C]can't forget the
day I shot that
bad bitch down

[Outro]
[C]Come on, you've
got to listen
[F]unto me
[D]Lay off that
whisky, and
[G]let that
cocaine
[C]be
title: Cocaine Blues
tuning: E A D G B E
